course_description:
Veterinary Technologists play an increasingly important role in patient care and the organisation of veterinary practices, or animal enterprises. This course will equip Veterinary Technology students with the essential knowledge and skills required for successful professional participation in the operations of a veterinary practice, hospital, or animal focused-organisation. The course will build on prior learning in animal handling, providing students with knowledge in the operation of animal-focused enterprises through direct participation in Animal Husbandry Work Integrated Learning (AHWIL). Enrolment in VETS2009 is restricted. Students MUST have received a passing grade for the pre-requisite course ANIM1120 and completed 20 days toward the AHWIL milestone to be permitted to enrol in this course. Student enquiries relating to eligibility for enrolment can be directed to the SVS Admin Team (vetenquiries@uq.edu.au) for assistance.

VETS2009 is designed to equip veterinary technology students for leadership roles in the management of a modern veterinary practice. Students completing VETS2009 will gain important skills in resource and financial management, veterinary reception management, practice marketing, human resources and healthy workplaces, animal behaviour and microchipping. Students will gain knowledge of relevant legislation related to Animal Care and Protection, Radiation Safety, safe use and storage of veterinary drugs. ﾠﾠﾠ

VETS2009 will provide fundamental training in Animal Husbandry Work Integrated Learning (AHWIL) in Veterinary Technology and Veterinary Nursing, by upskilling students in animal husbandry within working animal enterprises (veterinary clinics, animal production systems, research animal houses etc). The course will provide important foundations in how veterinary practices work from the perspective of a veterinary technologist and will provide further insight into animal welfare, animal ethics, and communication within a busy veterinary practice. Details of the academic program requirements for AHWIL are provided in the prerequisite course ANIM1120. ﾠ

Additional timetable information
As a condition of enrolment in VETS2009, you are required to complete a 5-day professional placement in a veterinary enterprise during the semester. Full attendance is required for the 5 days of placement at approximately 8hrs per shift (i.e.40 hours of placement). Any additional hours per day or a reduction in placement days requires prior approval from the Course Coordinator.
See
Learning Activities > Additional Learning Activity Information
for more information about Attendance and Absence.
Placements must be self-sourced and submitted for approval via UQ’s placement management system,
InPlace
.
Self-sourced placements must be registered via the VETS2009 Self Placement link on your InPlace dashboard within the following timeframes:
· A minimum of four (4) weeks prior to the placement start date for domestic placements (within Australia).
· A minimum of six (6) weeks prior to the placement start date for international placements (outside Australia) – more than 6 weeks’ notice is preferred.
If you require assistance sourcing a placement, contact
vetenquiries@uq.edu.au
to seek support from the SVS Placements Team. Include the following information in your request:
· Placement dates (as allocated within the course)
· Course code and any specific placement requirements
· Locations other than your normal semester residence in SI-net where you have access to free accommodation (e.g., staying with family or friends)
· Distance you can travel daily for your placement
· Interest / ability to relocate for the placement and support yourself with paid accommodation
· The type of clinic experience you are seeking for this placement (e.g., small animal General Practice, mixed animal General Practice, large animal General Practice)
The SVS Placements Team can provide assistance with sourcing placements within Australia only. All international placements are self-sourced by the student and subject to approval by the Course Coordinator and Head of School.
As a University of Queensland student you are bound by the
Student Code of Conduct
. You are representing the University and any misconduct (including on clinical placement) will be treated seriously and referred to the appropriate authorities. It is expected that you have read the Student Code of Conduct.

course_aims: This course aims to provide fundamentals of veterinary clinical practice operations, relevant legislations and financial aspects of management of clinical practice. At the end of the course, students will demonstrate a clear understanding of management, communication and client care within veterinary enterprises. Students will further be able to demonstrate skills in animal husbandry within the context of animal enterprises.

learning_outcomes.description: Demonstrate knowledge and competency in management of a veterinary practice, including client care, employee safety and welfare, financial management and management of animals under your care.

Be able to explain the codes and regulations governing effective operation of a veterinary practice, including those related to animal care and protection, codes of practice, radiation safety and relevant drug legislations.

Prepare for clinical practice through engagement in industry related practical experiences, demonstrating practical capabilities in animal husbandry and handling, developing insight into the business management associated with animal enterprises.

Demonstrate a professional approach to working with and communicating with different Industry Partners and clients in animal enterprises, in operating as a multidisciplinary team, succinct to health and safety requirements and local risk factors.

assessment_details.other_conditions: Student specific, Work integrated learning. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: Performance Assessment This within-course Animal Husbandry Work Integrated Learning (AHWIL) placement is designed to equip students for clinical placement in their 3rd year of the Veterinary Technology Program. The placement is the ultimate opportunity for students in their pre-clinic phase to demonstrate skills in animal husbandry, communication, professional attitudes and behaviours within veterinary contexts. For this assessment task, you will be required to attend 5 days of professional placement in a veterinary enterprise during the semester. This assessment task is built on prior learning and assessment, as follows: Completion of animal handling and professional training in pre-requisite courses for VETS2009, as outlined in the Course Information page of the Course Profile. Successful completion of 20 days of preliminary AHWIL, as required under the program rules of the Bachelor of Veterinary Technology. Thus, the total number of days that must be completed to pass VETS2009 will be 25 days, including this in-course AHWIL. Successful completion of Reflective Task A of the Assessment Sequence: Reflections on AHWIL, as outlined in the VETS2009 Course Profile. Credit applications for prior experience will not be considered for this work-integrated learning task. Student performance will be assessed via an assessment rubric, completed by providers of placement , in consultation with the Course Coordinator or their delegate. To pass this task, students must be graded as 'SATISFACTORY' in each of the five domains of activity on this placement. Details of the rubric and other information can be found in the file entitled 'VETS2009 Industry Placement Resource', posted to the VETS2009 Blackboard site. Additionally, it is a requirement of this course that students seek placements in a General Practice clinic placement, and not in a clinic in which they have completed their 20-days preliminary AHWIL. learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 1 To Week 12 (27 Jul - 25 Oct)
learning_activities.topic: Principles of Clinical Practice Lectures A series of lectures that will guide students to develop knowledge and competency in management of veterinary practices. The Lectures will include: Week 1: Indigenous Perspectives, Animal Care and Protection Act, The Code of Practice, Methods of Practice Week 2: Self and Animal Advocacy, Veterinary Practice Organization and Management Week 3: Veterinary Practice Organization, Operations and Management, Applied Ethical Practice Week 4: Vet Reception Fundamentals, Introduction to Drug Legislation, Managing a Vet Pharmacy, Drug Terminology and Abbreviations Week 5: Veterinary Practice Finances, HR Management and Healthy workplaces, Client Care and Customer Service Week 6: Euthanasia, Mental Health Well-Being, Workplace Health and Safety Week 7: Microchipping, Vet Practice Marketing, Third party Finance, Pet Insurance. Week 8: Behaviour and Puppy Pre-School Week 9: No Lectures Scheduled Week 10: No Lectures Scheduled Week 11: No Lectures Scheduled Week 12: Registration as a Vet Technologist or Vet Nurse

learning_activities.topic: Tutorials in Clinical Practice Week 2: Conflict Resolution in Veterinary Contexts Week 3: Team-Based Learning- Applied Ethics Week 5: Team-Based Learning- Reception Case Studies Week 6: Team-Based Learning- End of Life Discussions Week 7: Team-Based Learning- Pet Loss and Grief Week 8: Team-Based Learning- Sustainable Well-Being Week 8: Panel Discussions on Clinical Placements, Career Paths for Veterinary Technologists and Registration as a Vet Tech or Vet Nurse
